title: ASP.NET Core 10 — what's new
exp: You're already running a .NET 10 Web API on the SCIM project — that's a talking point most candidates don't have. Know what's new so you can say "I've used X directly."
pts: **OpenAPI 3.1:** JSON Schema 2020-12 aligned. Nullable types as type arrays (["string","null"]). Better compatibility with code generators
**IOpenApiDocumentProvider via DI:** access the generated OpenAPI schema outside an HTTP request — useful in background services or startup tooling
**Automatic memory pool eviction:** ASP.NET Core's internal memory pools now release memory back to OS during idle periods
**Passkey/WebAuthn in Identity:** built-in passwordless auth using device biometrics or hardware keys — no third-party library needed
**Tighter OpenTelemetry:** more built-in meters for request duration, queue depth, active connections

qa.q: What changed about OpenAPI generation in ASP.NET Core 10?
qa.a: It now produces OpenAPI 3.1 documents conforming to JSON Schema 2020-12. Nullable reference types are represented as a type array ["string","null"] instead of {type: "string", nullable: true}. This means client generators that expect strict JSON Schema compliance now work correctly without workarounds.

A new interface injectable via DI that lets you programmatically access the generated OpenAPI document outside an HTTP request context. Use cases: startup task that uploads your API schema to an API gateway, background service that validates the schema, or integration tests that inspect the generated document without making an HTTP call.

qa.q: How would you tie .NET 10 passkey support to your SCIM/SSO project in an interview?
qa.a: The SCIM system handles user lifecycle while SSO handles authentication. .NET 10's built-in passkey support means you could replace the password+JWT flow with WebAuthn using the same ASP.NET Core Identity framework you're already using — no third-party FIDO2 library. It's a direct extension of the auth work you're already doing.
